followUp.question: Sachet or tin?
followUp.hint: The filling machine and shelf life differ completely, and sachets dominate the mass market.

analysis.summary: Double concentrate (28 to 30 Brix) tomato paste in 70g form-fill-seal sachets, made from fresh field tomatoes.

materials.name: Fresh tomatoes
materials.role: Primary material. Ripe field tomatoes, 4 to 6 Brix.
materials.source: Kadawa irrigation scheme, Yankaba and Kwanar Gafan markets (Kano); also Jos, Kaduna, Katsina, Benue

materials.name: Salt and citric acid
materials.source: Local chemical dealers, Kano or Lagos

materials.name: Sachet laminate film
materials.role: Packaging. Printed BOPP/PE laminate roll stock for form-fill-seal.
materials.source: Lagos packaging converters (Agbara, Ikeja industrial estates)

process.title: Wash and sort
process.detail: Air bubble and water pressure clean the tomatoes. Remove unripe and rotten fruit.

process.title: Crush and break
process.detail: Hot break heats pulp to 85 to 90°C for 10 to 15 minutes; cold break to 55 to 60°C. Both stop pectinase. Hot break gives higher viscosity and a stronger red; cold break gives higher yield.

process.title: Pulp and refine
process.detail: A double-stage pulper reaches about 90% pulp yield, separating skins and seeds.

process.title: Evaporate
process.detail: The most energy-intensive step. Juice at 5% solids becomes 28 to 36% concentrate, under vacuum well below 100°C.

process.title: Fill and seal sachets
process.detail: The pouch machine codes, forms, meters, fills, seals, counts and cuts automatically.

equipment.name: Air bubble washer and sorting conveyor

context: Nigeria is the 14th largest tomato producer in the world, second in Africa, and grows about 65% of West Africa's tomatoes.
It still imports about 150,000 tonnes of tomato paste concentrate a year, worth about $170 million. Other estimates put it at 300,000 tonnes and $360 million, mostly from China.
Of roughly 1.5 million tonnes of tomatoes grown a year, around 900,000 tonnes rot for lack of storage, processing and transport.
A small line costs $20,000 to $100,000 and processes 200 to 500 kg of fresh tomatoes an hour. At ₦1,390/$, an $80,000 line is about ₦111m FOB, roughly ₦145m landed and installed.
Grades: 28 to 30 Brix (double concentrate) is the retail standard. 36 to 38 Brix (triple) is for industrial buyers and export.

cost.verdict: Local production is about 10% cheaper, but only inside the February to May harvest window with contracted farmgate supply. Off season, tomatoes reach ₦3,000/kg and local production costs three times the landed import price. At ₦145m installed and one 90-day campaign a year, break-even is roughly 11 million sachets: years, not months.
caveats: The tomato campaign lasts 60 to 90 days in most regions. The real limit on the line is how many tomatoes you can source every day of it.
Erisco Foods opened a tomato paste plant in February 2016 and closed it that November. Dangote's plant shut in 2017, reopened in 2019 and only became fully operational in February 2020.

Imported tomato paste is banned by the federal government and NAFDAC is enforcing it, though local makers say imports still flood the market. If enforcement holds, the import column becomes theoretical.
Equipment prices are supplier ranges, not quotes.

steps.title: Contract tomato supply
steps.detail: Agree farmgate supply through NATPAN and Kadawa growers for every day of the February to May campaign. Daily volume, not price, is what limits the line.

steps.title: Order the line
steps.detail: Get quotes from turnkey suppliers for a 500 kg/h line. Equipment lead time is the longest item in the plan.

steps.title: Register with NAFDAC
steps.detail: Product registration (₦50,000) and facility inspection run alongside the equipment order.

steps.title: Install and commission
steps.detail: Install the line, boiler and water treatment, then run test batches before the campaign opens.

steps.title: Wash, sort, crush and hot break
steps.detail: Take in 7.8 t of fresh tomatoes. Wash, remove unripe and rotten fruit, crush and hot break at 85 to 90°C.

steps.title: Pulp, evaporate and sterilise
steps.detail: Pulp to about 90% yield, evaporate under vacuum to 28 Brix, then UHT sterilise at 108 to 110°C.

steps.title: Fill, pasteurise and pack
steps.detail: Fill 20,000 70g sachets, pasteurise at 80°C, cool, code and pack 50 to a carton.

quotes.brief: 70g double concentrate tomato paste sachets, 28 to 30 Brix, hot break. 20,000 sachets per batch, three batches during the February to May campaign. Collection in Kano. Quote per sachet, your minimum order, and whether you can supply NAFDAC-compliant labelling.
